package_info.package_name: LockBit and Makop Ransomware Phishing Attachments
package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious Windows executables delivered via phishing)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package consists of phishing emails with compressed attachments containing executables disguised as benign files (PDF/JPEG). These executables, when run, perform ransomware operations including reconnaissance, obfuscation, persistence, file encryption, and ransom note creation. The delivery method and payload are designed to deceive users and cause significant harm.

execution_context.trigger: user-execution (after opening attachment and running disguised executable)
execution_context.file_location: NSIS-packed EXE inside compressed archive (disguised as PDF or JPEG)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Deletes Windows Volume Shadow Copies using: vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code invokes vssadmin.exe to delete all volume shadow copies, removing backup data and preventing easy recovery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deleting shadow copies is a common anti-recovery tactic used by ransomware to prevent victims from restoring files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely deletes all system backups without user consent; this is highly abnormal for any application.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup management tools may delete old shadow copies, but only with explicit user action.
key_indicators: Silent deletion of all shadow copies
Use of vssadmin.exe in a non-administrative tool

execution_context.file_location: NSIS-packed EXE inside compressed archive (disguised as PDF or JPEG)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Encrypts user files on the infected computer using ransomware-specific encryption routines.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code recursively enumerates files on the system, encrypts them with a ransomware algorithm, and appends a specific extension.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Mass file encryption is a hallmark of ransomware and is never performed by legitimate software without user intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not encrypt user files en masse without clear user action.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or archiving tools may encrypt files, but only with user configuration.

execution_context.file_location: NSIS-packed EXE inside compressed archive (disguised as PDF or JPEG)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Creates a ransom note TXT file in affected directories.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code writes a ransom note text file to directories containing encrypted files, instructing the victim on payment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Creation of ransom notes is a direct indicator of ransomware activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not create ransom demands or instructions for cryptocurrency payment.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; ransom notes are unique to extortion malware.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Performs system reconnaissance and persistence operations (details not fully disclosed, but includes process enumeration and registry modification).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates running processes and modifies system settings to maintain persistence and evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reconnaissance and persistence are common steps in malware to ensure successful execution and resistance to removal.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not enumerate processes or alter persistence mechanisms without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System management tools may perform similar actions, but with user consent and transparency.

attack_chain.action: Phishing email delivers a compressed attachment with a password, themed as a copyright claim.
User extracts and executes the disguised executable (PDF/JPEG icon).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code execution on the system.

attack_chain.action: Malware deletes volume shadow copies to prevent recovery.
Malware performs reconnaissance and persistence operations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware ensures it remains active and undetected.

attack_chain.action: Malware creates ransom note files in affected directories.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim is instructed to pay ransom for decryption.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of NSIS-packed EXE files from compressed email attachments
Immediate deletion of volume shadow copies via vssadmin.exe
Bulk file encryption and creation of ransom note TXT files
Process enumeration and registry modification for persistence
file_indicators: Executables with PDF or JPEG icons inside compressed archives
Ransom note TXT files in user directories
NSIS installer files with suspicious payloads
network_indicators: Potential C2 communication for key exchange or ransom instructions (not explicitly detailed in report)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of NSIS-packed executables from email attachments, especially those disguised as documents or images. Alert on use of vssadmin.exe to delete shadow copies, bulk file encryption activity, and creation of ransom note files. Flag emails with password-protected compressed attachments containing executables. Correlate with known IOCs (file hashes) and look for process behaviors indicative of ransomware.
